evidence: "\\(\\log ab - \\log|b| = \\log\\dfrac{ab}{|b|} = \\log|a|\\) (since \\(b/|b| = \\pm 1\\))." The stated reason is the only step that carries the question, and it does not deliver the answer: b/|b| = ±1 gives ab/|b| = ±a, i.e. \\(\\log(\\pm a)\\), not \\(\\log|a|\\). A student following the printed reason cannot get from ±a to |a|. The absolute value comes from the DOMAIN, which the solution never mentions: for \\(\\log ab\\) to be defined we need ab > 0, so a and b share a sign, and then ab/|b| = a·sign(b) = |a| in both cases.
proposedFix: Replace the parenthetical with the domain argument: "\\(\\log ab\\) is defined only when \\(ab > 0\\), so \\(a\\) and \\(b\\) have the same sign. Then \\(\\dfrac{ab}{|b|} = a\\cdot\\operatorname{sign}(b) = |a|\\) (if \\(b>0\\) then \\(a>0\\) and the value is \\(a=|a|\\); if \\(b<0\\) then \\(a<0\\) and the value is \\(-a=|a|\\)). Hence \\(\\log ab - \\log|b| = \\log|a|\\)."
